pull_request.title: Verify PE/COFF header construction in linux-bzimage builder
pull_request.body: Verify all eight handwritten pe_header functions under explicit setup ELF layout preconditions. Specify exact section fields, aligned layout arithmetic, optional-header fields, and the ordered 368-byte header representation.
pull_request.bodyHTML: Verify all eight handwritten pe_header functions under explicit setup ELF layout preconditions. Specify exact section fields, aligned layout arithmetic, optional-header fields, and the ordered 368-byte header representation.

+/// Little-endian bytes as implemented by core's uint_macros::to_le_bytes
+/// (`to_le().to_ne_bytes()`), independent of the host endianness. Source:
+/// Rust 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3), library/core/src/num/uint_macros.rs; the delegated

review_comments.body:
**Type:** reuse-existing-specifications
**Problem:** Both contracts inline little-endian byte decompositions that vstd already models byte-identically as `spec_u16_to_le_bytes`/`spec_u32_to_le_bytes` (`vstd/bytes.rs:25,117`, already consumed by its own `external_body` wrappers) — a second trust source for the same core functions that can drift. Define them as `ensures bytes@ == spec_u16_to_le_bytes(value)` and `ensures bytes@ == spec_u32_to_le_bytes(value)` after importing the vstd definitions. Note `returns spec_u16_to_le_bytes(value)` does not type-check here: the return type is `[u8; 2]` while the vstd model is `Seq<u8>`, so the equality belongs in `ensures` on the array's view.

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0
+//! Trusted specifications for xmas-elf 0.10.0's parsing and header access.
+//!
+//! The `getter!` macro in `src/program.rs` matches `Ph32`/`Ph64`, reads the
+//! corresponding field, and widens it to u64. `ElfFile::new` delegates to
+//! `header::parse_header`; `program_iter` constructs `ProgramIter` at index zero,
+//! whose `next` stops at the declared count or the first parsing error. Parsing
+//! and iteration models describe those external operations; they do not assert
+//! any caller-specific PE layout. Bounds and alignment panics are excluded only
+//! by their explicit predicates. The library implementation remains trusted.
+use vstd::{prelude::*, std_specs::iter::IteratorSpec};
+use xmas_elf::{
+    ElfFile,
+    header::{Class, Header, HeaderPt1, HeaderPt2, HeaderPt2_, Machine_, Type_ as HeaderType},
+    program::{Flags, ProgramHeader, ProgramHeader32, ProgramHeader64, Type_},
+};
+
+use super::slice::as_ptr_spec;
+
+verus! {
+
+#[verifier::external_type_specification]
+pub struct ExElfFile<'a>(ElfFile<'a>);
+
+#[verifier::external_type_specification]
+pub struct ExHeader<'a>(Header<'a>);
+
+// The identification fields stay opaque; header_class models the class getter.
+// No executable implementation is skipped by this opaque type proxy.
+#[verifier::external_type_specification]
+#[verifier::external_body]
